groups.name: TV antiheroes whose therapist scenes are central to the show
groups.explanation: Carrie Mathison (Homeland — psychiatric treatment is central), Walter White (Breaking Bad — therapy/counseling scenes), Don Draper (Mad Men — sessions with psychiatrists are recurring), and Tony Soprano (The Sopranos — Dr. Melfi therapy sessions are a structural pillar of the show) are all TV antiheroes or morally complex leads whose therapy or psychiatric treatment scenes are a defining narrative feature.

groups.name: Actors who won a Golden Globe for playing a TV character named after a shade of a color
groups.explanation: Claire Danes won a Golden Globe for Carrie Mathison (Homeland). Bryan Cranston won for Walter White (Breaking Bad — White). Michael C. Hall won for Dexter Morgan (Dexter — Morgan). Dominic West won for Jimmy McNulty (The Wire). NOTE: This group concept does not hold cleanly — replacing with a valid concept. These four actors — Claire Danes (Homeland), Bryan Cranston (Breaking Bad), Michael C. Hall (Dexter), and Dominic West (The Affair) — all won Golden Globe Awards for Best Actor or Actress in a Drama Series for cable or premium television roles.

groups.name: Non-English-language Netflix dramas set in a real country under political crisis
groups.explanation: Versailles (French-language, France), Occupied (Norwegian-language, Norway under Russian occupation), 1983 (Polish-language, alternate-history Poland), and Suburra: Blood on Rome (Italian-language, Italy) are all non-English-language prestige dramas available on Netflix set in a specific real country with a defined political or societal crisis as the central dramatic premise.
